Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. chapters.title_en: Named among the patient and the best

claims.statement_en: Dhul-Kifl is named together with Ismail and Idris, and each of them is described as one of the patient.
God says that He admitted them into His mercy, and that they were among the righteous.
Dhul-Kifl is named again, with Ismail and Alyasa, and each of them is described as one of the best.

chapters.summary_md: Dhul-Kifl is named with Ismail and Idris, each of them one of the patient [c1]. God admitted them into His mercy [c2]. He is named again with Ismail and Alyasa as one of the best [c3].
chapters.body_md:
Dhul-Kifl is named together with Ismail and Idris, and each of them is described as one of the patient [c1]. God says that He admitted them into His mercy, and that they were among the righteous [c2].

Dhul-Kifl is named again, with Ismail and Alyasa, and each of them is described as one of the best [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The Quran names Dhul-Kifl in short lists [c1][c3]. One list ends with a double statement: they are among the patient [c1] and God admitted them into His mercy as righteous [c2]. The other list gives one description, among the best [c3].
chapters.kids_md: God named Dhul-Kifl with Ismail and Idris and said each of them was patient [c1]. God took them into His mercy [c2]. In another place God named him with Ismail and Alyasa and said each was among the best [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the Quran can honour a person with a brief mention and a single quality, patience, and that this needs no story to explain it [c1]. Another is that the mention is joined to God's mercy [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: anything Dhul-Kifl did or said, where or when he lived, or to whom he was sent.
- Not established: whether the Quran calls him a prophet or a messenger. The verses name him in lists and describe him as patient, righteous and among the best, and do not give him either title.
- Not established: what the name refers to or why he is called by it.
- Not established: what he was patient in.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later writers named various figures as Dhul-Kifl, including some known from earlier scriptures, and disagreed about whether he was a prophet; none of these identifications is used here.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about this prophet. None is used in this draft.

Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Dhul-Kifl is identified by later writers with different figures (among them one called Ezekiel in earlier scriptures). These identifications disagree and none is used.
The only ayat in the inventory are 21:85-86 and 38:48; the draft is deliberately short, because the Quran says nothing more of him.
A scholar should check that 'one of the patient' and 'one of the best' are the right renderings, and that 'admitted into His mercy' fits the verb.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
